governance.attested_by: neiso-53 winter fuel-security adoption session 2026-07-07 (branch claude/neiso-winter-component-b-012p1j, G-24)
governance.note: neiso-53 = the neiso-50 keeper recipe (identical run_config, reliability-floor CSV, offer bands and flags: --commitment --reliability-floor --hydro-backfill-year 2024 --hydro-eia930-monthly --gas-hub-basis-daily --scarcity-price-overlay --tranche-startup-amortization) with the three NEISO winter fuel-security mechanisms TURNED ON: neiso_gas_coldsnap_derate (temperature-dependent non-dual-fuel gas-CC/CT availability derate, TDFOR) + neiso_winter_fuel_inventory (Component A: Nov-Mar oil-burn seasonal inventory budget) + neiso_winter_fuel_mustrun (Component B: fuel-secure COAL_BIT/ST_GAS winter must-run). All three are structurally-faithful, forward-derivable real ISO-NE winter mechanisms grounded in the Winter Reliability Program (FERC ER14-2407) -> Inventoried Energy Program (ER19-1428) -> OFSA operational posture and the NERC/FERC Winter Storm Elliott cold-weather forced-outage record. ADOPTION RATIONALE (owner decision 2026-07-07, rule 1): on the 2023-2025 backcast the three mechanisms are DORMANT on every scored/material metric -- C3c and C5b do not move and prices are byte-near-identical to the zero-mechanism ablation twin (2026-07-07-neiso53-winter-fuelsec-ablation) (Component B does commit the immaterial fuel-secure COAL fleet on cold days, see free_parameters, but that class is <0.3% of ISO load and moves nothing scored): the NEISO model's winter capacity is ample enough that a <=13%-on-8-cold-peak-hours gas derate creates no genuine reserve shortage, the dual-fuel oil-parity cap (~$258/MWh) holds the price ceiling, and Component A's oil budget (9.79 M MMBtu/month) is never approached (winter oil draw ~3.3 M MMBtu/month). They are adopted for FORWARD faithfulness -- they are real, forward-responsive market structure that binds in a colder forecast year (the derate and oil budget then price winter scarcity endogenously and lift the >$300 tail) -- kept per rule 1 (a real market behaviour stays in even when the backcast residual does not move). This is NOT a residual fit: every winter parameter is a measured/physical constant (see free_parameters below), provably tuned to no scored metric here since it moves none. The prior hypothesis that a missing winter commitment (Component B) or the coupled cold-snap derate closes the C3c/C5b caveat family is REFUTED for the 2023-2025 backcast; the residual is a NEISO winter capacity-adequacy / scarcity-price-formation gap, not a fuel-security-mechanism gap (G-24 struck with this evidence).
governance.validation_note: Reproducible from the committed bundle: scripts/replay_keeper.py results/calibration/neiso49_resolve_confirm --out-dir results/calibration/neiso53_winter_coldsnap_ab --set neiso_gas_coldsnap_derate=true --set neiso_winter_fuel_inventory=true --set neiso_winter_fuel_mustrun=true. ABLATION TWIN registered alongside (2026-07-07-neiso53-winter-fuelsec-ablation, all three mechanisms off = the neiso-50 baseline) -- this RESOLVES the neiso-50 audit_keepers.py E9 missing-twin flag noted in the prior keeper's attestation. D-3 attribution: the twin's prices/storage/oil-burn match this run within <1% every year (mechanisms inert), confirming Component B binds only on the IMMATERIAL fuel-secure COAL fleet (D-2 forced share 0.35/0.23/0.02 vs 0.0 in the twin; COAL is 0.04-0.2% of ISO load, reported-not-gated per rule 20 v2.1) and ST_GAS forced share is unchanged (0.124/0.827/0.398 both arms -- owned by the reliability netload limb; Component B drops ST_GAS to avoid stacking, rule 24); Component A and the cold-snap derate carry NO forced energy and move no scored metric on 2023-2025. Leave-one-year-out (rule 22): unchanged from neiso-50 -- no value was fitted to a single year's residual (the winter params are NERC/WRP physical constants, frozen against the residual, rule 23). Holdouts (2022, H1-2026) remain fully quarantined (rule 22). REMAINING OPEN C7 GATE (unchanged from neiso-50, SKIPPED/immaterial, ST_GAS <0.1% of ISO load, rubric v2.1): the ST_GAS diurnal-shape residual is a separate root cause not touched by this adoption.

The fast-start tranche pricing + econ-band re-anchor recovered a third of the gap ENDOGENOUSLY (0.74 -> 1.05 TWh, no storage-formulation change — per the neiso-ps-undercycling diagnosis, the PS number may only move downstream of price structure). DEEPENED by neiso-49 (honest cost, rule #1): the measured-cost ST_GAS committed tranche shaves the artificial evening peak the PS fleet was arbitraging; the residual spread is the same ledgered winter/scarcity price-formation gap, and per the neiso-ps-undercycling diagnosis it may only be recovered via price structure, never a storage knob.

entries.name: ST_GAS/CC_CHP measured-offer-band reach-ratio dependency (2026-07-06 addendum)
entries.where: results/calibration/neiso_stgas_netload (offer_curve_by_group ST_GAS + CC_CHP entries, same 72-scalar surface as the first ledger entry above)
entries.identification: derived-dependency (declares a coupling within already-counted scalars; not a new free parameter)
entries.source: The ST_GAS 0.79/0.85/0.89 and CC_CHP 1.15/1.17/1.19 bands are the NEISO-native CAMPD-measured marginal heat rate (ST_GAS 0.642/0.692/0.731; CC_CHP flat 0.94-0.97) multiplied by the NEISO-native CC reach ratio 1.223 (= CC_REGULAR econ_high 1.15 / native CC marginal HR 0.940). CC_REGULAR econ_high 1.15 is itself residual-identified (see the first ledger entry's offer_curve_by_group.value.CC_REGULAR.econ_high). So while the ST_GAS/CC_CHP bands are measured-grounded in level, the reach ratio that anchors them to the CC_REGULAR scale is not independent of that residual value.
entries.root_cause: wave-manager tranche review 2026-07-06 (#1498 deficiency 6, docs/handoffs/wave-manager-tranche-review-2026-07-06.md): dependency was undeclared at neiso-49's promotion. If CC_REGULAR econ_high (1.15) is ever re-identified (re-derived under a different residual fit), the reach ratio 1.223 changes, and the ST_GAS 0.79/0.85/0.89 and CC_CHP 1.15/1.17/1.19 bands re-derive with it — they are not independently anchored.

entries.citation: min_stable_pct 0.40 = subcritical steam-boiler turndown (Merrimack-class coal min-load ~40% nameplate); commit_frac 1.0 = the WRP/IEP fuel-secure steam fleet IS the program fleet; tmin_c -7C = NERC cold-weather forced-outage onset (~20 degF). Program driver: Winter Reliability Program FERC ER14-2407 -> IEP ER19-1428 -> OFSA. None tuned to the C1/C3c/C5b residual (rule 23 frozen). Component B BINDS on the immaterial fuel-secure COAL fleet (D-2 forced share 0.35/0.23/0.02 vs 0 in the twin; COAL <0.3% of ISO load, reported-not-gated per rule 20 v2.1, moves no scored metric); ST_GAS is dropped from Component B when the reliability netload limb is active (rule 24), so ST_GAS forced share is unchanged (owned by that limb).

entries.name: neiso_winter_fuel_inventory (Component A) + neiso_winter_fuel_start_fill_bbl
entries.citation: Nov-Mar oil-burn seasonal budget = start_fill x (1 + delivery_fills) / 5 months, MMBtu-correct over the oil-capable fleet (oil-primary + dual-fuel oil limb on switch hours). start_fill 2.8M bbl = Winter Reliability Program (FERC ER14-2407) 2014/15 low fleet oil-inventory target; delivery rate + tank autonomy from ISO-NE OFSA / WRP studies + EIA-860 (winter-fuel-inventory clean datatype). Forward-regenerable capacity/logistics quantities (rule 13), not measured receipts. Never tuned to the residual; monthly cap 9.79 M MMBtu is never approached (winter draw ~3.3 M/month).

entries.name: neiso_gas_coldsnap_derate + neiso_gas_derate_{t0_c,slope_per_c,cap}
entries.lineage_solves: adopted 2026-07-07 (G-24); <=13% cut on 8 cold-peak hours, moves no price
entries.citation: Temperature-dependent forced-outage of non-dual-fuel gas-CC/CT: frac = clip(slope*(t0-TMIN),0,cap) on the winter cold-snap peak hours, keyed to NEISO load-weighted daily TMIN. cap 0.20 = NERC/FERC Winter Storm Elliott (gas fuel-supply ~20% of unplanned outages, largest forced-out category); t0 -7C = NERC cold-onset; slope 0.018 = cap/(t0 - T_extreme). Forward-reproducible from pinned/forecast TMIN, condition-responsive, NOT fitted to the number of >$300 hours (produces zero here).
